newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KLSE puts trading limits on Paragon.
newsitem.headline: KLSE puts trading limits on Paragon.

text.p: The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) said on Friday that it has put trading limits on the stock of Paragon Union Bhd with effect from November 12.

In a statement, the KLSE said it had declared the shares "designated securities" which means, among other things, that a buyer of the stock would have to put down a 100 percent payment before entering the purchase contract.
Paragon Union's businesses include making car carpets and automotive components, precision machining and metal stamping. Its stock closed up 5.60 ringgit to 22.40 ringgit on Friday.

Under the restrictions, sellers must also first deliver shares of the company to the stockbroker before any sales are allowed. In normal trading, investors are allowed to buy and sell shares without taking delivery of scrip, as long as the transactions are concluded within seven market days.
The exchange has in the past imposed such restrictions to cool speculative excesses in stocks.
Officials at Paragon could not be reached for comment.
The KLSE last designated a stock in April, when it placed trading restrictions on Super Enterprise Bhd, a packaging and labelling company.
